thread:
olivia (support): Heads-up — Customer reported embeddings failing with a dimension error and a billing spike. Pasting their report and payload below.

olivia (support): Customer says they started seeing HTTP 400 from /v1/embeddings and then a sudden usage jump on their bill. They claim they didn't change model; using our 'text-embedding-3-large' (1536 dim).

olivia (support): Customer logs: `400 Bad Request "Invalid input shape: expected a list of strings or single string. Received nested arrays."` Also our logs show backend responded to that request with an EmbeddingDimensionMismatch error: `expected dim=1536 got=3072` for some batch.

olivia (support): Here's the exact payload they sent (redacted API key):

```json
{
  "model": "text-embedding-3-large",
  "input": [["doc1 part A", "doc1 part B"], ["doc2"]],
  "user": "acme-service"
}
```

olivia (support): They included this in a single API call. They said their client library flattens nested arrays inconsistently, and retry logic ended up re-wrapping the list.

matt (infra): OK. Two likely issues: 1) server-side validation should reject nested arrays earlier with a clear 400, 2) billing spike could be caused by client retries that duplicated requests or by our ingest counting each inner string separately if we unintentionally concatenated.

alex (embeddings): From the dimension error: getting 3072 suggests we treated one nested element as a single long input (2x1536) or concatenated two sub-doc strings into a single embedding request without proper splitting. Example: if the client sent `[ ["a","b"], ["c"] ]` and our batching flattened to `["a","b","c"]` but then the client retried with the nested form, we might have attempted to embed the nested array as a single JSON value, resulting in doubled tokenization.

olivia (support): Customer says their client is JS using a custom wrapper. They pasted the failing curl they ran: 

```bash
curl https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-large","input":[["title","body"],["single doc"]]}'
```

olivia (support): And the server returned: `{"error":{"message":"Invalid embedding dimension: expected 1536, got 3072","type":"invalid_request_error"}}`

matt (infra): Can we reproduce locally? alex, can you run a quick job against staging with that nested shape and see how runtime handles it and whether billing metrics increment?

alex (embeddings): Reproduced on staging. If the `input` field is a nested array, our JSON decoder currently accepts it (it's valid JSON), then the runtime tries to coerce elements. We have two code paths: per-item embedding and batch-serialization. In this case it created a single concatenated input for the first nested element: `["title","body"]` -> converted to `"[\"title\",\"body\"]"` and tokenized as a longer string. That produced an embedding vector of expected dimension, but because we later attempted to stack vectors we hit a shape mismatch when mixing normal and concatenated items. The net error becomes dimension mismatch.

alex (embeddings): Short repro steps I ran:
1) curl to staging with `input=[["a","b"],["c"]]` -> get 400 / dimension mismatch.
2) curl with `input=["a","b","c"]` -> success (3 embeddings).
3) curl with `input=["a\nb","c"]` (single string combining parts) -> success (2 embeddings) but different tokenization.

olivia (support): Customer also said their SDK retry logic sent the same payload 3x over 10s when encountering 400s, which explains the billing spike because retries were counted. They attached timestamps that match three successful-ish ops on our side (we accepted and processed them in staging-like environment).

matt (infra): For next steps:
- Add stricter top-level validation returning `400 Invalid input: must be string or list of strings` before runtime batching.
- Emit a clear error code for nested-arrays so SDKs can detect and fix client-side.
- Add a small telemetry flag to mark these requests so we can identify affected customers and offer billing adjustments.

alex (embeddings): Agreed. Quick mitigation I can push to staging in ~30m: validate JSON `input` type strictly (string or array of strings only, no nested arrays). I'll also add a debug metric `embedding.request.invalid_shape:nested_array` to help find impacted accounts.

olivia (support): Meanwhile I replied to the customer suggesting they change payload to a flat list (one embedding input per entry) and to update retry logic to not retry 4xxs. I included this example fix: 

Correct payload examples:
```json
// multiple docs
{
  "model": "text-embedding-3-large",
  "input": ["doc1 title - doc1 body","doc2 full text"]
}

// single doc
{
  "model": "text-embedding-3-large",
  "input": "single document text here"
}
```

olivia (support): Also offered to investigate billing and asked for the exact timestamps of the spikes.

matt (infra): If the customer provides the timestamps, we can query accounting telemetry and if it's clearly caused by our glitch/ambiguous error, we'll consider a one-time credit. Also we should check whether the ingest pipeline deduplicates repeated request IDs; if not, add guidance in docs.

alex (embeddings): One more note — for SDK authors: prefer flattening into array-of-strings before sending, and avoid embedding client-side nested arrays without explicit concat semantics. We'll add a snippet in docs and a note in the changelog.

olivia (support): Customer replied quickly and sent timestamps (they're in PST): 2026-03-10T15:02:12Z, 2026-03-10T15:02:19Z, 2026-03-10T15:02:26Z. They also attached their SDK version which does have a known bug in v0.9.2 that causes double-wrapping of lists during retry.

olivia (support): I logged a ticket with Billing & Docs. Tagging for follow-up: matt, alex — will keep thread updated. :thumbsup:

embed-bot: deploy-check: staging validation rule added for nested-array input? pending PR #1427.

matt (infra): I'll coordinate a small billing review if we see the spike is > $50 for the customer. If it's systemic we'll do a broader sweep.

alex (embeddings): PR opened and running unit tests that validate input types. If CI green I'll push to canary later today. Will post back with logs showing `embedding.request.invalid_shape:nested_array` counts after rollout.

olivia (support): Thanks team — marking as escalating until billing decision made. I'll send the customer the flat-payload workaround and a temporary mitigation note for their devs.

olivia (support): Action items: 1) alex push validation to staging/canary 2) matt check billing telemetry & prepare possible credit 3) docs to add example and a short note about client-side shapes.

olivia (support): Closing internal loop once PR lands and billing decision done.
